title: Token-maxxing is dead, OpenRouter's token usage plateaus
content:
Rankings data by OpenRouter is licensed under CC BY 4.0. Reuse and republish it with attribution. The Data API docs cover the citation format and JSON access to these datasets.
Live LLM rankings by real-world usage. Models are ranked by tokens processed through the OpenRouter API by millions of developers. View all text models
Usage data through
Each model is ranked by the number of tokens it processed through the OpenRouter API, counting both prompt and completion tokens. Usage is aggregated into daily buckets in UTC and totalled per model variant, so variants of the same model, such as a free variant, are ranked separately. Requests that a user or app keeps private are excluded before aggregation.
Today, This Week, and This Month each cover a trailing window of one day, seven days, and thirty days, ending with the most recent complete daily bucket. Trending compares the trailing seven days with the seven days before it and ranks models by the percentage change in tokens, including only models with at least one million tokens in the current window so that a small base cannot produce a large percentage. New models with no prior week are listed first, up to five of them.
The date above the rankings is the newest usage bucket the leaderboard is computed from, not the time the page was rendered or deployed, so it advances only when new usage data is aggregated.
These rankings show traffic routed through OpenRouter. The Top Models chart and the LLM Leaderboard rank models by tokens processed, while the Market Share chart counts requests. None of them measures users or spend. Models differ in verbosity and tokenization, so a higher token total shows how much a model is used, not which model is best for a task. They do not rank models by accuracy, reasoning ability, or benchmark performance. The Benchmarks section ranks those using scores from Artificial Analysis and Design Arena, plus benchmarks such as GPQA Diamond that OpenRouter runs itself and reports as median accuracy across providers. For coding, compare the Artificial Analysis Coding Index there with the Programming section, which ranks models by tokens on a sample of requests in a chosen language, such as Python. The Top Models chart names the nine most-used models in each period and groups the rest as Others. The Market Share chart shows each model author's share of text requests on OpenRouter, with the remaining authors grouped as Others.
Text summary of the Today tab of the leaderboard above. Models are ranked by tokens processed on OpenRouter over the most recent complete day, with the change measured against the day before it.
Text summary of the This Month tab of the leaderboard above. Models are ranked by tokens processed on OpenRouter over the trailing thirty days, with the change measured against the thirty days before them.
Text summary of the New & Trending tab of the leaderboard above. Models are ranked by the percentage change in tokens processed over the trailing seven days against the seven days before, among models with at least one million tokens in the current week. A model with no prior week is marked new.
Text summary of the Market Share chart above. Share of text requests made on OpenRouter in the week beginning Oct 12, 2026, with the change in each author's requests against the week before it. DeepSeek leads at 24.4% of the week's requests. Authors the chart groups as others are listed last, so the rows match the series the chart plots.
Summary of the context-length chart above for the 10K context window in the week beginning Oct 12, 2026. Others leads with 2b requests.

report.summary: OpenRouter's live usage data suggests token-volume growth has plateaued, signaling that raw token consumption is no longer a reliable proxy for AI adoption or model value.
report.background: OpenRouter aggregates real-world LLM API traffic from millions of developers and ranks models by tokens processed, requests, and market share. Its leaderboard has become a public observability layer for which models teams actually use. The phrase 'token-maxxing' describes an industry habit of treating token volume as a proxy for adoption, capability, or progress: more tokens processed means more usage, more value, more AI. But OpenRouter's rankings explicitly warn that tokens are not users or spend, and that models differ in verbosity and tokenization. If token totals flatten while request share shifts, it suggests the market is optimizing for efficiency, cost, and task fit rather than raw output volume.
key_points: Token totals are flattening: OpenRouter's trailing-day, weekly, and monthly rankings show token throughput growth slowing or plateauing, undermining the idea that ever-higher token consumption is a reliable growth signal for AI products.

Tokens are not users or spend: the leaderboard counts prompt and completion tokens, not unique users or dollars. Verbosity and tokenization differences mean a model can lead on tokens without being the most used, cheapest, or best for a task.

Request share tells a different story: OpenRouter's Market Share chart counts requests, and DeepSeek leads at 24.4% of text requests in the week beginning Oct 12, 2026, suggesting price and efficiency can drive adoption more than raw token volume.

Short-context workloads dominate: the context-length chart for the 10K window shows 'Others' leading with 2 billion requests, indicating most real traffic is short-context rather than long-context token-heavy usage.

Trending still moves: the New & Trending tab ranks models by percentage change in tokens with a one-million-token floor, and new models are listed first, showing that share can shift quickly even when aggregate token growth stalls.
report.impact: For the AI industry, a token-usage plateau shifts attention from raw volume to cost per successful outcome, latency, and reliability. Developers should instrument token efficiency, use prompt caching and routing, and avoid treating verbose outputs as progress. Model providers may compete less on token generation and more on task accuracy, price, and context discipline. Regular users benefit from cheaper, faster, and less bloated responses, but they should also be wary of vendors citing token totals as proof of adoption. OpenRouter's public data is useful, but it measures routed traffic, not the whole market or business value.
report.tools: Follow OpenRouter Rankings and its Data API (CC BY 4.0) for token, request, and market-share trends. Pair it with Artificial Analysis for benchmark and coding-index comparisons. For token and cost observability in your own stack, try Helicone, Langfuse, or LiteLLM; add prompt caching and model routing to reduce token spend without sacrificing quality.
